text.p: Transkaryotic Therapies Inc said Wednesday it has begun treatment of the first patient in its Fabry disease clinical trial.
The Phase I trial is being conducted at the National Institutes of Health and is expected to enroll 10 patients.

Fabry disease is a genetic disorder caused by deficient activity of the enzyme alpha-galactosidase A (alpha-gal A). In Fabry disease, a toxic compound accumulates throughout various organs and tissues of the body due to the deficiency of alpha-gal A.
"As a first step in developing a gene therapy treatment for Fabry disease, TKT scientists have produced a purified form of the alpha-gal A protein," the company said.
"After the safety of the protein is established, we then intend to treat patients with their own cells, genetically-engineered to produce the missing protein."
Founded in 1988, TKT has developed two proprietary technology platforms, gene activation and gene therapy.

The company said its gene activation technology is a proprietary approach to the large scale production of therapeutic proteins which does not require the cloning of genes and their subsequent insertion into non-human cell lines.
TKT said its most advanced gene activation development program is for the production of gene-activated erythropoietin with clinical trials expected to commence in the first half of 1997.
The company's collaborative partner for these trials is Hoechst AG Hoechst Marion Roussel Inc subsidiary.
